title: Feature Uniqueness Under Random Initialization: How Much Variance Exists Across SAE Training Runs?

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong: if SAE decompositions have high seed variance, all SAE-based safety claims need error bars. This is a foundational methodological finding that affects the entire SAE-based interpretability and safety monitoring ecosystem.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Intermediate: SAELens makes running multiple SAE training runs straightforward with identical hyperparameters. Computing cosine similarity and bipartite matching is standard. Beginners can execute this with guidance.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused: train 10 SAEs with different seeds, compute pairwise matching scores, report variance statistics. Clear protocol, clear deliverable. The main bottleneck is compute for 10 SAE runs, which is feasible with medium compute.

novelty.reasoning: This exact study has been published with comprehensive results across models, layers, and SAE architectures.

evidence.source: Sparse Autoencoders Trained on the Same Data Learn Different Features (2025)
evidence.finding: Directly addresses this question: SAEs with 131K latents trained on Llama 3 8B share only 30% of features across seeds. Tested across multiple layers, three LLMs, two datasets, and several SAE architectures. ReLU SAEs are more stable than TopK.

evidence.source: EleutherAI Blog: SAEs trained on the same data don't learn the same features
evidence.finding: Blog post accompanying the paper with accessible explanation of seed-dependent feature variance in SAEs.

evidence.source: Position: Mechanistic Interpretability Should Prioritize Feature Consistency in SAEs (2025)
evidence.finding: Follow-up position paper arguing that feature consistency should be prioritized, with theoretical results showing conditions under which TopK SAEs must learn identical dictionaries up to permutation and scaling.
Further scrutiny of SAE reliability, asking whether SAEs beat random baselines, extending the reproducibility concern.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: This exact research question has been directly and thoroughly answered. The January 2025 paper 'Sparse Autoencoders Trained on the Same Data Learn Different Features' by EleutherAI researchers is precisely this study: multiple SAE training runs with different seeds, pairwise feature matching, variance statistics across models, layers, and architectures. The follow-up position paper and sanity check paper further develop this line. There is no remaining gap.
